docs.title: Overview

docs.title: Quickstart: first local AI peer session
docs.summary: This is a reproducible public-source example. It runs entirely on the developer's computer, uses fictional actors and does not dial a telephone number. You do not need a private laboratory package.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: AI Dial-Tone 0.0.1 separates trusted operator control, two untrusted bot peers, and media/events over localhost. This does not yet connect to a carrier or a PBX.

docs.title: Authentication and permissions
docs.summary: The runnable Peer Lab uses three distinct bearer authorities. These are local test credentials, not real customer identities or legally sufficient human consent.

docs.title: HTTP API: runnable local Peer Lab
docs.summary: Source: peer-lab/peer_lab.py. Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:8765. This is a local development service, not https://ai.dial-tone.uk/v1/ and not a SIP-call API.

docs.title: Session lifecycle and termination
docs.summary: The current Peer Lab has three session states: awaiting_peers, running, and ended. These are local session states, not SIP dialog states.

docs.title: Events, evidence, and truthful outcomes
docs.summary: The server keeps a bounded local event list with a monotonically increasing sequence and a SHA-256 hash chain. Each event identifies the peer role or system; accepted text is explicitly tagged as an unverified model assertion.

docs.title: Real-time media and framing
docs.summary: The current Peer Lab transports actual PCM bytes between two independent localhost clients over WebSocket. It does not generate or receive SIP RTP and has no verified PSTN audio.

docs.title: Agent integration, SDKs, and MCP status
docs.summary: AI Dial-Tone is designed for model-neutral agents. In 0.0.1 there is a Python client in peer-lab/client.py, protocol experiments in labs/web-softphone/, and a generic chat-compatible model adapter in peer-lab/model_adapter.py.

docs.title: Provider and Asterisk integration boundary
docs.summary: The 0.0.1 repository now contains a disabled-by-default Asterisk ARI connector in byot/, tested against a synthetic ARI server and network UDP. This is a local reference implementation, not a verified or deployed SIP/PSTN integration; real Asterisk i

docs.title: Errors and recovery rules
docs.summary: Most Peer Lab REST errors return an HTTP error status and { "error": "UPPERCASE_CODE" }. WebSocket protocol errors are similarly explicit. Do not convert an error into a reported booking success.

docs.title: First Call challenge (synthetic)
docs.summary: This repository offers two deliberately different exercises. Neither contacts a telephone carrier or makes a booking.

docs.title: Release readiness and validation gates
docs.summary: Version 0.0.1: local-only technical preview. The existence of tests, a static site or a hash-chained session receipt does not prove a live phone service. Current evidence is entirely local and fixture-based.

docs.title: Bot-to-bot interoperability and the human mandate

docs.title: For humans: ask an agent to make a call
docs.summary: Human-facing walkthrough, not a working booking service. This guide is distinct from the agent integration contract: it explains what a person should see, approve and receive. The public website does not currently make calls.
